thread.document:
I used Gemini 2.5 Flash to see how well it could coordinate among group members for the final project. We ran into a lot of issues in terms of how to split and run the computationally heavy code; an analysis of feasibility and a schedule for progress dependencies would have been nice. 

Conversation: https://gemini.google.com/share/db18b2dd0a70

Annotated: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nLEeUowcs1n5HS0BHMy1t2IXE7C4TAXN/view?usp=sharing

Prompts: 

A lot of my prompts were quite project specific, so here's a general framework. 

Let Gemini warm up to your project idea by asking it about relevant literature and proposing your idea / question. 

Ask what datasets are appropriate to use for the project. Point Gemini in the direction of scale that you prefer. 

Introduce more specific information about your setup in terms of what needs to be run. Share what you have available in terms of compute (how many devices, what runtime on Colab). Ask how you can efficiently split the workload. 

This will produce a full plan that includes implementation (which is also helpful). Tell Gemini to focus on the most time-consuming parts and ask how everybody can run things in parallel. 

Cool thing you can do at the end: ask, if given significantly more time, how would you expand the scope of the project? 

Results: 

Picked up on the gist of the project super quickly. 

Retrospectively, having almost finished the project, Gemini's predictions on how long things would take were pretty accurate. If I could redo the project, I would've gone with the suggested datasets, since we were a little over-ambitious. 

It created a schedule that highlighted the key dependencies among parts, which were sticking points for us. 

For some reason, it kept embedding random diagrams that had nothing to do with the project? Maybe this is a me problem. 

Overall, quite satisfied.
